Let

\[
p(\lambda)=(1-\alpha\lambda)(1-\beta\lambda)
=1-(\alpha+\beta)\lambda+\alpha\beta\lambda^2.
\]

We need minimize \(\max |p(\lambda)|\) on \([1,2]\cup[4,8]\).

The key lower bound comes from the three points \(1,\frac92,8\), all in the allowed set. For every quadratic \(p(\lambda)=1-s\lambda+t\lambda^2\),

\[
\frac{72}{49}p(1)-\frac{32}{49}p\!\left(\frac92\right)+\frac{9}{49}p(8)=1.
\]

Thus, if \(|p|\le r\) on the two intervals, then

\[
1\le \left(\frac{72}{49}+\frac{32}{49}+\frac{9}{49}\right)r
=\frac{113}{49}r,
\]

so

\[
r\ge \frac{49}{113}.
\]

Equality forces the signs and magnitudes to align:

\[
p(1)=\frac{49}{113},\qquad
p\!\left(\frac92\right)=-\frac{49}{113},\qquad
p(8)=\frac{49}{113}.
\]

Solving gives

\[
p(\lambda)=1-\frac{72}{113}\lambda+\frac{8}{113}\lambda^2.
\]

Indeed,

\[
p(\lambda)=\frac{8}{113}\left(\lambda-\frac92\right)^2-\frac{49}{113},
\]

so on \([1,2]\cup[4,8]\) its maximum absolute value is exactly \(\frac{49}{113}\): it equals \(+\frac{49}{113}\) at \(\lambda=1,8\), and \(-\frac{49}{113}\) at \(\lambda=\frac92\).

Now match coefficients:

\[
\alpha+\beta=\frac{72}{113},\qquad \alpha\beta=\frac{8}{113}.
\]

So \(\alpha,\beta\) are the roots of

\[
x^2-\frac{72}{113}x+\frac{8}{113}=0,
\]

hence

\[
\alpha,\beta
=
\frac{36\pm 14\sqrt2}{113}.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{\frac{49}{113}},
\]

attained exactly for the unordered pair

\[
\boxed{\left\{\frac{36+14\sqrt2}{113},\frac{36-14\sqrt2}{113}\right\}}.
\]
